Fix video playback becoming unavailable after watching several videos.

- Handle YouTube's `LOGIN_REQUIRED` response as a playback authorization failure instead of trying to turn a response without streams into a DASH manifest.
- When a connected YouTube account exists, retry an anonymous playback denial exactly once through a separate authenticated, player-capable session. This corrects the previous behavior where playback was always anonymous even when the account was connected, so reconnecting by itself had no effect.
- Preserve the signed-in visitor context rather than overwriting it with BotGuard's anonymous visitor identity. Keep per-video proof-of-origin tokens and player script deciphering available for adaptive/SABR streaming.
- Keep the authenticated player session isolated from account browsing and invalidate it on account switch, sign-out or language change.
- If YouTube also rejects authenticated playback, display an actionable authorization error instead of a misleading manifest error or an endless retry loop. Some provider-side restrictions may still require verification in the browser.
- Add regression tests for working playback, authenticated fallback, double rejection, missing formats and request failures.

Validation: core tests, TypeScript checks and Windows/Linux packaging in CI. A live authenticated YouTube playback test on the affected Windows system is still recommended because upstream anti-bot decisions depend on the account, video and network.

Windows x64 and Linux x64 (AppImage/DEB) installers include source and automatic-update metadata. Windows installers remain unsigned.
